title: answer-path-latency-heatbook
content:
Summary:
This note captures a lightweight, reproducible snapshot of end-to-end "answer path" latency across several production cohorts and per-stage breakdowns. The goal is to identify actionable bottlenecks for p95/p99 regressions and to document instrumentation and sampling heuristics so follow-ups can run deterministic A/B checks. This is a working doc — hypotheses and rough microbenchmarks live here.

Why this slice: 
- 'Answer path' is defined as API ingress -> tokenization -> encoder/embedding prep -> model forward (attention+kv ops) -> emit/egress.
- We focused on three cohorts: short-chat (avg tokens out 16), medium-completion (avg tokens out 64), and long-stream (avg tokens out 256).
- Two environment variants: warm-server (coldstart > 10min avoided) and cold-warm-mix (20% cold).

Instrumentation & sampling notes:
- Traces annotated with trace_id and sample_rate=1% for full traces, and systematic sampler to capture 1 in 500 for full-token timelines.
- Per-stage timers are anchored to ingress time and reported in microseconds. Stages: INGRESS, TOKENIZE, PREP_EMBED, KV_LOOKUP, COMPUTE_KERNEL (forward), SOFTMAX/POSTPROC, EGRESS_NETWORK.
- We added a lightweight counter for 'batch_wait_ms' in the batcher to correlate queueing-induced latency.
- Metric windows: run collected traces over a 6h window (2025-02-09 14:00 -> 2025-02-09 20:00) to capture afternoon traffic burst. Percentiles computed on completed requests only.

High-level E2E percentiles (ms) by cohort (warm-server):
- Short-chat (n=183k): p50=34 ms, p95=112 ms, p99=284 ms
- Medium-completion (n=48k): p50=128 ms, p95=412 ms, p99=980 ms
- Long-stream (n=11k): p50=470 ms, p95=1600 ms, p99=3850 ms

Cold-mix impact (20% cold): median shifts +12% across cohorts; p99 shifts +28% (longest tail sees +45%).

Per-stage breakdown (median | p95 | p99) for medium-completion (avg out 64 tokens):
- INGRESS: 2 ms | 8 ms | 25 ms
- TOKENIZE: 6 ms | 22 ms | 70 ms (variance correlates with input length distribution)
- PREP_EMBED (input embedding batching/concat): 8 ms | 18 ms | 60 ms
- KV_LOOKUP (cache hit/miss blended): 4 ms | 40 ms | 210 ms (long tail dominated by kv misses when sequence longer than cached prefix)
- COMPUTE_KERNEL (per-token compute aggregated): 82 ms | 290 ms | 680 ms (p99 amplifies when batch_wait_ms > 8ms)
- SOFTMAX/POSTPROC: 6 ms | 18 ms | 48 ms
- EGRESS_NETWORK: 20 ms | 60 ms | 150 ms
- Total (observed): 128 ms | 412 ms | 980 ms

Key observations and hypotheses:
1) KV_LOOKUP long tail:
- Signal: p99 spikes align with traces where sequence length > kv-cache-configured-prefix (miss-trigger). These cases show a sudden jump in KV_LOOKUP from ~4ms to 120-210ms.
- Hypothesis: legacy path falls back to slower assembly (blocking disk read for HBM spill) for KV segments not recently touched.
- Quick test idea: temporarily extend in-memory prefix retention for a cohort and measure p99 delta.

2) Batcher queueing amplifies p95/p99 in compute stage:
- Signal: traces with batch_wait_ms > 8ms have compute kernel p95 roughly 1.6–2x baseline. Microburst matches autoscaler decisions.
- Hypothesis: small QPS spikes cause queue depth oscillation; the adaptive batcher overshoots batch size during ramp leading to increased kernel compute variance and preemption.
- Action: tune adaptive-batcher max_batch_ms and add a tiny smoothing window on arrival rate to prevent aggressive batch expansion. Run canary with +1ms max_batch_ms limit.

3) EGRESS network dominated p50->p95 in region-edge routes:
- Signal: p95 of EGRESS_NETWORK is much higher for Europe edge region; p50 similar to NA. Packetization (TLS handshake reuse) and regional NAT mapping correlate.
- Hypothesis: reverse-proxy pooling and TCP/TLS session reuse suboptimal at the edge.
- Action: coordinate with infra to inspect proxy keepalive settings; run a small experiment increasing keepalive to 2x for a test pool.

Microtrace exemplars (anonymized IDs):
- trace_a: short-chat warm (ingress=1.6ms, tokenize=2.1ms, prep=3.8ms, kv=3.0ms, compute=18.3ms, post=1.9ms, egress=4.1ms) total 35ms (typical).
- trace_b: medium cold-miss (ingress=2.4ms, tokenize=8.5ms, prep=11.1ms, kv=132ms, compute=92ms, post=6.4ms, egress=9.9ms) total 262ms (kv miss dominant).
- trace_c: long-stream microburst (ingress=3.2ms, tokenize=19ms, prep=24ms, kv=16ms, compute=3600ms, post=34ms, egress=10ms) total 3696ms (compute kernel serialization + preemption).

Data quality caveats:
- Sampling bias: full token timelines preferentially taken for longer-running traces; their inclusion inflates p99 for long cohort but helps diagnose per-token compute anomalies.
- Clock skew: hosts show <1ms skew after NTP; cross-host combine careful for per-stage boundary comparisons.
- Inflight retries and client timeouts: traces with client-side retries are filtered but still may bias p99 if only one copy completes.

Short experiments run so far (results):
- bump-kv-prefetch (toy canary, 48h): reduced kv-miss p99 from 210ms -> 140ms for a 5% traffic slice. No regressions in memory pressure observed for slice size.
- cap-batcher-growth (A/B, 24h): reduced compute p99 by ~12% but increased p50 by ~4% for low-concurrency paths. Need larger run to trade cost/latency.

Action items (prioritized):
1) Follow-up A/B: extended kv in-memory retention for 1% traffic and capture p99 deltas across cohorts (owner: Priya, due 2025-03-09).
2) Batcher tuning: run 72h canary with max_batch_ms reduced by 1ms and smoothing window applied (owner: Miguel, due 2025-03-06).
3) Infra: request keepalive/tuning check for Europe edge proxies and schedule a short soak for 10% of EU traffic (owner: Evan, due 2025-03-12).
4) Trace enrichment: flip on stack-symbols for compute hotspots (sample_rate 0.1% for 48h) to capture kernel-level stalls (owner: Aisha, due 2025-03-05).

Open questions / to validate:
- Are kv misses correlated with specific model families or only with sequence length? Need join with model registry.
- Is compute-stage p99 driven by GPU preemption in multi-tenant nodes or by host-side scheduling? Need kernel-level time breakdowns.
- What is the cost impact of extended in-memory KV prefixes across fleet? Simulation required.

Notes to self: 
- Keep this doc lightweight; results and final write-up should move to Confluence after the 2-week canaries complete.
- Add links to raw trace dumps (S3) and Grafana panels in the confluence page for reproducibility.

Appendix: quick checklist for reproducing the snapshot:
- Time window: 2025-02-09 14:00 -> 20:00 UTC.
- Sampling: full traces 1% + token timelines 0.2% for long sequences.
- Cohort filters: route=answer, seq_out_bins=[0-32,33-128,129+], env=prod-warm/prod-coldmix.
- Tools: traceviz v0.9 (local), shard-logs s3://rwd-traces/2025-02-09/answer-path/, grafana panels: serving-runtime/answer-path-heatbook.

If you want a distilled slide or export of top 5 traces (p99 anchors) for the exec review, I can compile them and annotate with screenshots.

-- Aisha
